blocks.html: A string is a sequence of characters such as a name, a sentence or a password: "Patna" ,
"Class 11-A" , "Pass@123" . C++ supports two kinds of strings:

items.html: The string class (from <string> ) — modern, safe and easy. Used in this book.

items.html: cin >> s; reads only one word (stops at a space).

blocks.html: Common mistake: After cin >> n; the Enter key stays in the input. A following getline then reads an empty line. Fix it with cin.ignore(); before getline .
Each character has an index starting from 0.

items.html: s[0] is 'H'; s[s.length() - 1] is the last character 'O'.
s.at(i) is like s[i] but gives an error message if i is out of range (safer).
Unlike Python, C++ has no negative indexing; s[-1] is wrong.
C++ strings are mutable: you can change a character, e.g. s[0] = 'J'; (Python strings cannot be changed).

blocks.html: 1. Differentiate between cin >> s and getline(cin, s) .
Answer: cin >> s reads characters only up to the first space (one word). getline(cin, s) reads the entire line, including spaces, until Enter is pressed.
2. Why is cin.ignore() used before getline() ?
Answer: After cin >> number , the newline from the Enter key remains in the input buffer. getline() would read that empty line. cin.ignore() removes the leftover newline.

5. Differentiate between string class and C-style strings (two points).
Answer: The string class grows automatically and supports + and == directly; C-style strings are fixed-size char arrays ending in '\0' and need strcat() and strcmp() .
6. Write a code segment to count the letter 'a' in a string.
7. What is the use of replace() and insert() ? Give an example of each.
Answer: replace(pos, n, str) replaces n characters starting at pos: "I love Patna".replace(7, 5, "Bihar") → "I love Bihar". insert(pos, str) inserts text:
"Patna".insert(5, " City") → "Patna City".
8. Convert the first letter of a string to uppercase. Write the code.
Answer: s[0] = toupper(s[0]); — for "hello" this gives "Hello".
